title: MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment Length
summary: Learn the MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment length, three-task structure, timing strategy, marking process, and session-specific grade boundaries.
body_markdown:
The **MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment length is 2 hours** . It is one on-screen examination taken near the end of MYP Year 5, not three separate papers. During those 120 minutes, students complete three broad tasks that assess mathematical knowledge, investigation, communication, and real-life application.


The official duration does not include computer setup, identity checks, or invigilator instructions. Approved access arrangements are handled separately, so candidates should confirm their exact schedule with their school’s IB coordinator.


### How long is the MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment?


The official examination duration is **120 minutes** . Standard Mathematics and Extended Mathematics have the same examination length, although Extended Mathematics covers additional content and greater mathematical depth.


The IB may refer to the standard pathway simply as **Mathematics** . Schools and revision platforms often use **Standard Mathematics** to distinguish it clearly from Extended Mathematics.


Examination task Main assessment focus Approximate marks Suggested time


Knowing and understanding Criteria A and C 31-35 About 40 minutes


Investigating patterns Criteria B and C 31-35 About 40 minutes


Applying mathematics in real-life contexts Criteria D and C 31-35 About 40 minutes


The 40-minute division is a **timing recommendation** , not an IB requirement. Students may need longer for a demanding investigation or modelling response, but they should avoid spending so long on one task that another remains incomplete.


Students should not assume that separate reading time will be added. The published working time is two hours, while session instructions and authorized access arrangements are administered by the school.


### What is assessed during the two-hour examination?


Questions draw on the programme’s broad mathematical branches: **number** , **algebra** , **geometry and trigonometry** , and **statistics and probability** . Students may need to calculate, graph, generalize, interpret, model, justify, or evaluate rather than provide only short numerical answers.


### Task 1: Knowing and understanding


This task primarily assesses **Criterion A** , supported by **Criterion C** . Students choose appropriate mathematical methods, apply them accurately, and communicate enough working for an examiner to follow the solution.


A correct final answer does not always demonstrate every assessed skill. Substitutions, intermediate steps, notation, units, and explanations may earn marks or show partial progress when an answer is incomplete.


### Task 2: Investigating patterns


This task focuses mainly on **Criterion B** and also assesses **Criterion C** . Students may identify a pattern, test cases, formulate a general rule, verify it, and justify why it works.


Merely stating a rule is often insufficient. Strong responses connect the rule to mathematical evidence and use precise notation instead of relying on unsupported observations.


### Task 3: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts


This task focuses mainly on **Criterion D** , again supported by **Criterion C** . Students apply mathematics to a realistic context, interpret their results, evaluate assumptions, and consider whether a model is reasonable.


For example, a student might calculate dimensions for a design and then explain whether the result is practical or limited by the available information. The[official IB Mathematics subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief-mathematics-en.pdf) connects these task types to the four criteria. RevisionDojo’s guide to[how MYP Mathematics is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) provides a student-focused explanation.


### How the MYP Mathematics eAssessment is graded


Classroom MYP assessment and external eAssessment use related criteria but different calculations. In classroom assessment, teachers commonly award achievement levels from **0 to 8** for four criteria, producing a total out of 32.


The external eAssessment does not apply that classroom conversion directly. IB examiners award **raw marks** using examination markschemes, and the total is converted to a grade from **1 to 7** through subject- and session-specific boundaries.


Criterion Main focus Approximate weighting


**A: Knowing and understanding** Selecting and applying mathematical methods 25%


**B: Investigating patterns** Forming, verifying, and justifying general rules 25%


**C: Communicating** Using notation, representations, and reasoning clearly 25% across all tasks


**D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts** Modelling, interpreting, and evaluating results 25%


The examination has **100 marks overall** , with approximately 25 marks associated with each criterion. Criterion C appears across all three tasks rather than in one isolated communication section. Small variations in task totals are possible while the overall criterion weighting remains balanced.


Consider a hypothetical student who receives 20/25 for A, 18/25 for B, 19/25 for C, and 17/25 for D. The raw total would be **74/100** , which the IB would compare with the official boundaries for that examination session.


If a hypothetical session placed the grade 6 boundary at 70 and grade 7 at 82, that student would receive grade 6. These figures are illustrative, not predicted boundaries. RevisionDojo’s guides to[MYP grade boundaries](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-myp-grade-boundaries-understanding-the-1-7-scale) and[good MYP scores](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-a-good-myp-score-understanding-the-ib-middle-years-programme-grading) explain why classroom totals and eAssessment results should not be converted in the same way.


### Does a percentage guarantee a particular MYP grade?


No fixed percentage guarantees a grade in every session. **MYP Standard Mathematics grade boundaries are session-specific** , so previous boundaries provide context but cannot predict a later conversion with certainty.


MYP assessment is criterion-related rather than norm-referenced. Students are assessed against defined achievement standards, not placed into grades according to a predetermined proportion of candidates. Boundaries may change when papers differ in demand, while the intended standard for each grade remains comparable.


For the full MYP certificate, Mathematics contributes one grade from **1 to 7** . Certificate candidates must earn at least **grade 3 in each required eAssessment component** , obtain at least **28 points out of 56** , and satisfy the school’s service requirements. These conditions are separate from school rules for passing an internal course.


### A practical two-hour timing plan


A useful starting point is three flexible 40-minute blocks:


- Spend approximately **5 minutes** reading the task, identifying required outputs, and selecting relevant information.
- Use roughly **25-30 minutes** for calculations, investigation, reasoning, or modelling.
- Reserve **5-10 minutes** to check accuracy and improve notation, labels, units, explanations, and conclusions.


If a question takes too long, record meaningful progress and continue. A correct formula, substitution, diagram, pattern, or justified assumption may earn marks even without a final answer.


Pay close attention to command terms. **Calculate** requires an appropriate result and working, while **justify** , **verify** , and **evaluate** require explicit reasoning. Calculations alone may leave Criteria B, C, or D underdeveloped.


### How to prepare for the examination length


Complete at least one full **two-hour mock examination** under realistic conditions. Short topic sessions develop knowledge, but they do not fully test concentration, time management, or the ability to produce a sustained modelling response near the end of the examination.


Use the[MYP Standard Mathematics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics/questionbank) for targeted practice, then move to timed papers through the broader[MYP Standard Mathematics resource collection](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics) . After each attempt, classify lost marks by criterion rather than recording only a percentage.


Look for inaccurate methods under Criterion A, unsupported generalizations under B, unclear working under C, and weak interpretation or evaluation under D. Students deciding between pathways can also review the comparison of[Standard and Extended Mathematics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-myp-mathematics-extended-mathematics-vs-standard-mathematics) , although both examinations last two hours.


### Common mistakes about the examination


The assessment is not three separate 40-minute papers. It is one **two-hour on-screen examination** containing three major task types.


Communication is also not a separate final section. Criterion C applies throughout, so notation, labelled representations, coherent working, and explanations matter in every task. Students should also avoid applying the classroom 32-point table directly to an official raw examination mark.


### Conclusion


The **MYP Standard Mathematics eAssessment lasts two hours** and contains tasks on knowledge, pattern investigation, and real-life application. All four criteria are equally weighted, communication is assessed throughout, and raw marks are converted to a 1-7 grade using session-specific boundaries.


Preparation should combine mathematical knowledge with timed reasoning and modelling. RevisionDojo’s Questionbank, Study Notes, Mock Exams, and Jojo AI can support this work, with a complete two-hour practice paper as the most useful final rehearsal.
